newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January offshore banking unit assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January offshore banking unit assets rise.

text.p: The combined assets of Taiwan's 66 offshore banking units (OBU) grew 13.3 percent to hit a new high of US$36.675 billion at the end of January from a year earlier, the central bank said on Saturday.
About 77 percent of the assets, held by 36 local banks and 30 foreign banks, came from Asia, and the rest were from Europe and America, the bank said in a statement.
It added that the bank had recently approved three more OBU applications for foreign banks and one more for a local bank.
In January, Taiwan's OBUs reported a monthly foreign exchange turnover of US$4.817 billion, the statement said.

Of the derivatives operated by the OBUs, margin trading accounted for US$179 million, options took US$157 million, interest rate swaps took US$98 million, and financial futures accounted for US$82 million.

The government has planned to expand the OBU business as part of its scheme to become a regional financial centre. This expansion, although its size is currently unspecified, would herald some tax burden for OBUs, officials have said.
